p.docTitle:
Federal Act
on the Control of the Trade in Precious Metals
and Precious Metal Articles
(Precious Metals Control Act, PMCA)
Amended by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act of 28 Aug. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1).

preamble.p: The Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation,

based on Articles 95 paragraph 1 and 97 paragraph 1 of the Federal Constitution
SR 101 ,
Amended by No I 14 of the FA of 17 Dec. 2021 on the Harmonisation of Secondary Criminal Law with the Amended Law on Sanctions, in force since 1 July 2023 (AS 2023 254; BBl 2018 2827).
and having examined the Federal Council Dispatch dated 8 June 1931
BBl 1931 I 888A

level.heading:
Precious metal,
precious metal articles and multi-metal articles

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Precious metals under this Act are gold, silver, platinum and palladium.
Melt products are ingots, slabs, bars and granules produced by melting or recasting precious metal or melt material.

item.p: precious metals obtained through the extraction of raw materials or refining;
waste products from the processing of precious metals or alloys thereof which are usable for reclaiming precious metal;
material containing precious metal which is usable for reclaiming precious metal.

content.p: Precious metal articles are articles wholly comprised of precious metals with a legal standard of fineness, or articles made of precious metals with a legal standard of fineness in combination with a non-metallic material. This does not include coins made of precious metals.
Multi-metal articles are articles made of a combination of precious metal with a legal standard of fineness and base metals.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Plated articles are articles for which a layer of precious metal is fixed or plated to a substrate of another material.

The minimum requirements for precious metal layers are set out in Annex 1 hereto. The Federal Council shall specify the error tolerance and may adjust the provisions in the Annex in line with international developments.

item.p: articles made of precious metals that are below the minimum legal standard of fineness or do not satisfy the other material conditions for precious metal articles;
articles that qualify as multi-metal articles or plated articles but which are not marked as such or do not satisfy the material conditions for these categories of articles.

level.heading:
Legal standards of fineness
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Fineness refers to the purity of precious metal contained in a unit of weight of a metal alloy, measured in parts per thousand.

The legal standards of fineness for precious metal articles and multi-metal articles are set out in Annex 2 hereto. The Federal Council may adjust these provisions in line with international developments.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, with effect from 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p:
The Federal Council
Expression in accordance with No II of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033). This amendment has been made throughout the text. shall define the extent to which and the circumstances in which error tolerances may be allowed for deviations from the standard of fineness.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Where the Act or the Ordinance prescribes or authorises marks on goods, these must refer to the composition of the article. It is prohibited to apply a mark that is likely to be misleading to precious metal articles, multi-metal articles, plated articles or imitations or to items likely to be confused with these.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Precious metal articles may only be placed on the market with a legal fineness mark.
All parts of a precious metal article must at least meet the specified fineness. The Central Office for Precious Metals Control (Central Office) may make exceptions on technical grounds.
In addition to the fineness mark, articles of platinum or palladium must also bear a reference to the type of precious metal used.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Multi-metal articles may be traded as such provided that they are marked accordingly and satisfy the material conditions.
The actual composition must be clear from the mark. The precious metal parts must be clearly marked with the legal fineness in parts per thousand, the other metal parts with the type of metal used.
The different metals must be visible from the exterior and differ in colour. Multi-metal articles must not have the appearance of plated articles.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Plated articles may be traded as such provided that they are marked accordingly and satisfy the material conditions.
Plated articles must bear quality marks which must not leave any doubt as to their plated nature.
Imitations with precious metal coatings may be marked as gilded, silvered, platinised or palladised articles.
Plated articles and imitations must not bear any fineness marks.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: The Federal Council may prescribe or authorise other marks for precious metal articles, multi-metal articles, plated articles and imitations.
The Federal Council may provide for exceptions to the legally prescribed marks for special, i.e. technical and medical, purposes.
The Central Office may issue more specific provisions on the type and form of the prescribed and authorised marks.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: The Federal Council shall issue detailed provisions on the requirements for precious metal articles, multi-metal articles and plated articles.
It may authorise the Central Office to specify the technical details.

In addition to the prescribed marks, precious metal articles, multi-metal articles and plated articles must also bear a responsibility mark.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

Manufacturers who do not themselves produce the articles that they use may have their trademark stamped as a responsibility mark on the articles manufactured for them. Articles 10 to 12 apply in the case of these marks.

For watch-cases, members of manufacturer associations may use a collective responsibility mark with a serial number.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).
An indication of the standard of fineness may not be applied unless a responsibility mark is applied at the same time.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act of 28 Aug. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1).

content.p: The responsibility mark is a symbol which in itself identifies the owner of the mark. It may consist of letters, figures, words, graphic representations or artistic forms, individually or in combination. The mark should not be likely to be confused with previously registered marks or with the official hallmarks.
The imprint of the responsibility mark on the article must be clear and indelible.

The responsibility mark must be submitted in writing to the Central Office
Expression in accordance with No II of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033). This amendment has been made throughout the text. for registration. The application must include the owner’s place of residence and registered office and a precise description of the type of business as well as the evidence needed to prove the mark’s compliance with legal requirements.

An owner of a mark who is not listed in the Swiss Commercial Register or is not resident in Switzerland may be asked to provide collateral. This collateral serves as a guarantee for all claims under this Act.
The registration fee is payable on submission of the application.

The Central Office shall maintain a register of all responsibility marks that fulfil the legal requirements. The applicant shall be notified of the registration decision by registered letter, which, in the case of refusal, contains information on the right of appeal against the decision.

Registration applies for a period of 20 years from the date of registration. Before expiry of this period, it may be extended for a further 20 years at a time on payment of the relevant fee.
Inserted by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act 28 Aug. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1).

If, subsequently, the legal requirements for registration of a responsibility mark no longer apply, or if the registration period expires before an application for extension is submitted, the responsibility mark shall be deleted from the register.
Amended by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act 28 Aug. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1). A mark may also be deleted from the register if the owner uses it in contravention of this Act. Deletion shall be ordered by the Central Office and the owner of the mark shall be notified by registered letter, which contains information on the right of appeal.

...
Repealed by Annex No 135 of the Administrative Court Act of 17 June 2005, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Watch-cases made of precious metal are subject to an official control before being placed on the market. The control must be applied for by the manufacturer or the party who places the watch-case on the market.
For all other precious metal articles and for multi-metal articles, the owner of the articles may apply for an official control.
The official control covers the accuracy and the permissibility of the marks stamped on the articles.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: The accuracy of the fineness and responsibility marks stamped on the precious metal articles and multi-metal articles is certified by stamping the official hallmark.
Hallmarks bear the unique identification of the Assay Office conducting the official control.

The official control is applied for by written application to the relevant Assay Office. Only articles bearing a legal fineness mark and the responsibility mark may be controlled. The official control is certified by the official hallmark.

If the article submitted for controlling does not satisfy the legal minimum fineness or if the fineness mark stamped on the article does not match the actual fineness, the Assay Office shall refuse to grant its official hallmark and shall notify the Central Office, which shall order a second opinion.
Depending on the outcome of the second opinion, the Central Office shall either authorise the official hallmarking or it shall have the articles seized and shall file a criminal complaint.

If the objection is justified but no offence appears to have been committed, the Central Office shall take the steps necessary for the further processing of the articles in question, which may not be placed on the market in Switzerland. The costs thereby incurred are borne by the party submitting the article for controlling. The Central Office may order the destruction of the articles.
For all articles submitted for an official control, a fee (control or hallmark fee) must be paid irrespective of the outcome of the control.

For collection of the fees and expenses to be paid, a right of retention applies to the goods submitted for official control. In the event of dispute, claims are ruled upon by the Central Office. …
Sentence repealed by Annex No 135 of the Administrative Court Act of 17 June 2005, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

The Federal Council shall regulate the details of the procedure to be followed by the Assay Offices, the shape and composition of the official hallmarks, the means of notification of the official hallmark in Switzerland and abroad, the running of the controls and the amount of the fees, which must not be of fiscal character.

Articles manufactured abroad and governed by this Act may only be placed on the domestic market if they comply with the provisions of this Act. The requirement for the official controlling of the watch-cases mentioned in Article 13 paragraph 1 is extended to imported finished watches with such cases.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

The Federal Council may provide for exceptions for special articles.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

The articles governed by this Act may be subject to comprehensive or random testing on import. If such testing reveals a that an offence has been committed, the article must be seized and forwarded to the Central Office so that it may file a criminal complaint. If the article does not meet the statutory requirements but no offence has been committed, it shall be returned across the border.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

Watch-cases and watches subject to mandatory official controlling must be forwarded by the customs office conducting the import assessment to the appropriate Assay Office.
Amended by Annex No 19 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1411; BBl 2004 567).

In the case of travel samples which are imported by sales representatives in observance of the Federal Act of 1 October 1925

AS 2007 1411 Art. 131 para.1]. See now: Customs Act of 18 March 2005 (SR 631.0). on Customs and Commercial Treaties but which do not remain in Switzerland, the provisions may be relaxed if a reciprocity agreement exists with the country of origin.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: Precious metal articles, multi-metal articles, plated articles and imitations intended for export must bear the prescribed marks; in addition, watch-cases made of precious metal must also bear the prescribed official hallmark.
However, domestic manufacturers may, of their own accord, provide such articles with marks that are customary or prescribed in the destination country.

The Federal Council shall determine the requirements to be observed and the symbols used that the Assay Offices are permitted to use to confirm a standard of fineness as prescribed by the destination country.
The Federal Council may define relaxed provisions for watch-cases that are verifiably exported directly to countries which stipulate mandatory controlling of watch-cases.

Goods in direct transit may undergo an official control. Article 20 paragraph 3 applies correspondingly.
Amended by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act of 28 Aug. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1).

However, the provisions of this Act apply to those articles that do not enter the domestic market and remain under customs supervision, but which are forwarded abroad with Swiss transport papers duty unpaid.

For the removal of articles from customs or bonded warehouses, Art. 20, 21 and 22 paragraph 2 apply correspondingly.
Amended by Annex No 19 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1411; BBl 2004 567).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Art. 75 No 2 of the Trademark Protection Act of 28 Aug. 1992 (AS 1993 274; BBl 1991 I 1). Amended by Annex No 6 of the FA of 22 June 2007, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2551; BBl 2006 1).

content.p: If the Central Office suspects that imported, exported or transit articles unjustifiably bear or imitate a responsibility mark, maker’s or assayer’s mark that is not their own or that the provisions for the protection of intellectual property are violated in any other way, it shall notify the aggrieved party. The articles may be retained.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p: The hawking of articles subject to this Act is prohibited. This ban also applies to the taking of orders by retail sales representatives.

chapter.heading:
Trade in Melt Products and Melt Material
Amended by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).

content.p: Authorisation is required for the commercial manufacture of melt products.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).

content.p:
Individuals, commercial enterprises and cooperatives established under the Code of Obligations
SR 220 as well as comparable foreign enterprises may apply for a melter’s licence.
Amended by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).
Individuals must be entered in the Swiss Commercial Register and have their place of residence in Switzerland. They must be of good standing and offer proof of irreproachable business operations.

Commercial enterprises and cooperatives as well as Swiss branches of foreign enterprises must be entered in the Swiss commercial register. The persons entrusted with the administration and business management of the enterprises companies and cooperatives must be of good standing and offer proof of irreproachable business operations.

The melter’s licence shall on application be granted by the Central Office for a period of four years. On expiry of this period, the licence may be renewed provided that the applicant satisfies the statutory requirements.
Amended by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).

If a licence holder no longer satisfies any one of these requirements or has repeatedly violated the obligations assumed, the licence shall be automatically withdrawn by the issuing authority on a temporary or permanent basis.

Notice of the granting or withdrawal of a melter’s licence shall be given in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
Amended by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).

...
Repealed by Annex No 135 of the Administrative Court Act of 17 June 2005, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

Repealed by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, with effect from 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).
Repealed by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, with effect from 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033).
Repealed by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, with effect from 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).

level.heading:
Obligations of the licence holder.
Marking

content.p: Each melt product must be inscribed with the licence holder’s mark. The die used for the mark must be deposited with the Central Office and may not be changed without the approval of this body. Notice of the deposit of the die must be published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
The Federal Council shall specify the obligations of the holder of a melter’s licence.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

content.p: Any person who commercially purchases melt material within the meaning of Article 1 paragraph 3 letter b or c must ascertain the origin of the goods and document this.
If this person is entered in the Swiss commercial register, he or she must register with the Central Office.

If this person is not entered in the Swiss commercial register, he or she must obtain a purchase licence from the Central Office. This shall be granted if there is a guarantee of irreproachable business conduct.
Article 26 applies by analogy to the granting, renewal and withdrawal of the purchase licence.

The Federal Council shall define commercial purchases in more detail; in doing so, it shall in particular take account of the money laundering and terrorist financing risks posed by such purchases. It shall regulate the details of the due diligence and documentation duties.
Paragraphs 1 to 5 do not apply to holders of a melter's licence in accordance with Article 24.

level.heading: Determination of the fineness of melt products

content.p: Only Assay Offices or trade assayers may determine the fineness of melt products.
The control must determine the actual fineness of the melt product.

The controlling agency shall first establish that a mark has been stamped in accordance with Article 31. If not, the melt product shall be seized and the party requesting the determination reported. The case shall at the same time be referred to the Central Office, which shall ask the applicant to provide proof of origin of the melt product. If such proof cannot be furnished, or if there is any indication that an offence has been committed, the Central Office shall file a criminal complaint.

If the melt product has been stamped, the control shall be conducted. Once determined, the melt product is stamped with the mark of the Assay Office or trade assayer; the actual fineness must be specified at the same time.

The Federal Council shall regulate the details of the procedure for granting, renewing and withdrawing melter's and purchase licences and for fineness determinations.
Amended by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451). It may also issue regulations on the recognition of foreign official fineness determinations.
Amended by No I 5 of the FA of 21 Dec. 2007 on the Abolition and Simplification of Licensing Procedures, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 2265; BBl 2007 315).
The Federal Council shall regulate the fees to be paid for the official duties set out in paragraph 1. Article 18 paragraph 2 applies correspondingly.

The Central Office is affiliated to the Federal Department of Finance
Name in accordance with Art. 1 of the unpublished FCD of 23 April 1980 on the adaptation of federal law enactments to the new names of the Departments and Offices. This amendment has been made throughout the text. for the implementation of this Act. It may be incorporated into an existing administrative unit within the Department.
The Federal Council shall regulate the organisation of the Central Office.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

content.p:
The Central Office shall supervise the trade in precious metals and precious metal articles in accordance with this Act and the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 10 October 1997
SR 955.0 (AMLA).

item.p: register the responsibility marks;
supervise the official controlling and hallmarking of precious metal articles;
grant melter's and purchase licences;
keep the register of people who purchase melt material on a commercial basis;
supervise the commercial purchase of melt material;
supervise the determination of the fineness of melt products;
supervise the administration of the Assay Offices and the trade assayers;
issue the diplomas for sworn assayers and the assayer licences for trade assayers.

content.p: It shall collect fees for its supervisory activities concerning the trade in precious metals and precious metal articles, as well as a supervisory levy for the costs of the activities under paragraph 2 letter e and under Article 42ter that are not covered by the fees. The supervisory levy for the activities under paragraph 2 letter e shall be collected as a lump sum for a period of four years. The total assets and gross revenue shall be used as the basis for assessing the annual supervisory levy for activities under Article 42ter. The Federal Council shall regulate the details of the fees and the supervisory levy.

The Assay Offices for precious metal articles shall be established by the cantons or by the communes or business associations authorised to do so by the cantons. Establishment requires the approval of the Federal Department of Finance. It may also order the dissolution of an Assay Office if its facilities and management do not comply with the existing regulations or if there is no further need for its existence. The cost of establishing and operating an Assay Office shall be borne by the authorities or associations authorised to establish it. These shall receive the fees charged by the Assay Office.

In agreement with the appropriate cantonal government, the Department may establish federal Assay Offices if this is necessary in the country’s economic interests. In this case, the participating business sectors may be called on to contribute to the costs of establishment and any operating deficit of the Assay Offices. These Assay Offices report directly to the Central Office. The fees they receive flow into the federal budget.
The organisation, fees, accounting and operations of all Assay Offices are regulated by the Federal Council.

The Assay Offices deal with the official controlling and hallmarking of precious metal articles. They may also determine the fineness of melt products. Assay Offices may be assigned a limited geographical area in which to operate. They are authorised to control the precious metal articles and melt products made in that area. The Central Office may make exceptions under certain circumstances. The Assay Offices are prohibited from trading in melt material and melt products or performing any melting on behalf of third parties. Under certain circumstances, however, the Federal Department of Finance may authorise them to carry out such melting.

The Assay Offices shall support the Central Office in its supervision of enforcement of this Act. In particular, they shall report to it all offences that come to their attention and take the necessary measures to establish the facts by themselves or as instructed by the Central Office or the police authorities.
Officers of the Assay Offices are bound to secrecy concerning all observations made in the course of their work or which, by virtue of their nature, are confidential.

For losses incurred through incorrect execution of the duties entrusted to the Assay Offices, the Confederation shall be liable in the case of federal Assay Offices, and the canton in all other cases, to the extent that the bodies at fault cannot bear the costs themselves.

level.heading:
Official sworn assayers
Term in accordance with No II of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033). This change has been made throughout the text.

content.p:
Officers of the Assay Offices responsible for controlling the precious metal articles and multi-metal articles to be officially hallmarked and for determination of the fineness of melt products must hold a federal diploma as sworn assayers.
Amended by No I of the FA of 17 June 1994, in force since 1 Aug. 1995 (AS 1995 3102; BBl 1993 II 1033). This shall be issued by the Central Office on their passing the diploma examination. The assayer thus qualified shall swear an oath or make solemn promise before the Central Office to faithfully discharge the official duties of the profession.
The requirements for the acquisition of the federal diploma are determined by the Federal Council.

It is the duty of sworn assayers to comply with the provisions of this Act, the implementing provisions and the directives of the Central Office and avoid anything that could encourage others to commit an offence. Specifically, they may only perform fineness tests on melt products when the statutory requirements therefor have been met in each case and must immediately report all offences and administrative infringements under this Act that come to their attention. Article 38 paragraph 3 applies correspondingly.

The Central Office shall supervise the work done by the sworn assayers. It may withdraw the diploma in the event of serious violations of the duties incumbent upon the holder of an assayer diploma or on account of proven incompetence. …
Sentenced repealed by Annex No 135 of the Administrative Court Act of 17 June 2005, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).
Sworn assayers are liable for all losses or damage caused by the incorrect or negligent execution of their work. Article 38 paragraph 4 also applies.

level.heading:
Assayer licence.
Term in accordance with Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451). This change has been made in the provisions specified in the AS.
Duties

content.p:
Trade assayers must hold an assayer licence as trade assayer issued by the Central Office. This licence shall only be granted to assayers who hold a federal assayer’s diploma, are resident in Switzerland and are of good character. Trade assayers are permitted to acquire a melter's licence or purchase licence.
Third sentence amended by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451). Trade assayers shall swear an oath or make a solemn promise before the Central Office to faithfully discharge the official duties of their profession. They are authorised to ascertain the fineness of melt products and receive by way of remuneration the fees provided for in the Implementing Ordinance. They are not authorised to perform the official assaying and hallmarking of precious metal articles.

It is the duty of trade assayers to keep a proper account of the determinations of fineness that they perform and all sums received in return. For the purposes of official investigations, the Central Office and the police authorities may inspect the books and enquire about specific entries. The bookkeeping rules shall be drawn up by the Federal Council.
Article 40 applies correspondingly. The withdrawal of an assayer’s diploma means the withdrawal of the assayer licence as trade assayer.

level.heading: Additional licence for trading in banking precious metals

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex No II 11 of the Financial Institutions Act of 15 June 2018 (AS 2018 5247, 2019 4631; BBl 2015 8901). Amended by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

content.p: Trade assayers who themselves or through a group company trade on a commercial basis in banking precious metals require a licence from the Central Office.

blockList.listIntroduction: The licence shall be granted to trade assayers if:

item.p: they are entered in the commercial register as a commercial company;
they enjoy a good reputation and guarantee compliance with their duties in accordance with the AMLA;
the persons responsible for their administration and management also fulfil the requirements set out under letter c; and
their qualified participants enjoy a good reputation and guarantee that their influence is not detrimental to prudent and sound business operations.

content.p: If a company trades commercially in banking precious metals of a trade assayer that belongs to its group of companies, it also requires a licence. The requirements under paragraph 2 must be met.

level.heading: Supervision of trading in banking precious metals

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

content.p:
Licence holders in accordance with Article 42bis are subject to supervision by the Central Office in accordance with Article 12 letter bter of the AMLA
SR 955.0 .
The Central Office shall carry out the audits of licence holders itself or have them carried out by an independent and suitably qualified person (audit agent).

Article 24a paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 25 paragraph 1, Articles 29 to 33, 34, 36 to 38, 39 paragraph 1, Articles 40, 41, 42 and 42a of the Financial Market Supervision Act of 22 June 2007
SR 956.1 (FINMASA) apply by analogy. The audit agents and investigating agents are bound by official secrecy.

The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security

content.p:
The Federal Act of 22 March 1974
SR 313.0 on Administrative Criminal Law applies to the offences under Articles 56a to 56e. The prosecuting and adjudicating authority is the Federal Department of Finance.

Where a court judgment has been requested, or where the Federal Department of Finance considers that the requirements for a custodial sentence or a custodial measure are met, the offence is subject to federal jurisdiction. In such a case, the Federal Department of Finance shall refer the files to the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland for proceedings before the Federal Criminal Court. The referral is deemed to be the bringing of charges. Articles 73 to 83 of the Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law apply by analogy.
The representatives of the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland and of the Federal Department of Finance are not required to appear in person at the main hearing.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).

content.p: Where a criminal case is subject to the jurisdiction of both the Federal Department of Finance and the federal or cantonal courts, the Federal Department of Finance may order the prosecution to be unified under the prosecuting authority already dealing with the case, provided there is a close factual connection, the case is not yet pending before the competent court and the unification does not unreasonably delay the ongoing proceedings.

The Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court shall decide on any disputes between the Federal Department of Finance and the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland or the cantonal authorities.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex 1 No 3 of the FA of 19 March 2021, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2021 656; 2022 551; BBl 2019 5451).
